info.name: SmartFoodOps API
info.description:
Every route the Nginx gateway exposes across all 8 services (user, restaurant, menu, order, payment, rider, orchestrator, ai), organised and asserted the same way scripts/smoke-test.sh drives them: happy path, authorisation boundaries, edge cases, and the Temporal-driven order saga end to end.

**Run order matters.** Folders 1-11 are numbered because later ones depend on variables (tokens, ids) captured by earlier ones. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner, top to bottom, in one sitting -- individual folders can be re-run later, but only after folder 2 has populated tokens in this session.

**Folders 7 and 8 contain self-looping poll requests** (they re-send themselves via `postman.setNextRequest` until the order reaches the status they're waiting on, up to a bounded number of tries) -- since Week 2 the order lifecycle is driven by a Temporal saga, so a status is reached *eventually*, not by the time the request that triggered it returns. These only work in the Collection Runner, not on a single Send click; set a ~2000ms delay between requests there.

**Two things smoke-test.sh checks that this collection can't**: it reads three tables directly (payments, order_tracking_logs, riders) via `docker exec` to assert refunds, trail rows and fleet-leak invariants no HTTP response exposes, and it drives three compensation paths (no rider available, kitchen at capacity, and a permanently-failed refund) that need direct database or container manipulation to set up. Both are read-only observations layered on top of the same HTTP contract this collection already exercises.

See readme/observability-and-eventing-guide.md and readme/order-saga-orchestration-guide.md for how the pieces underneath these routes actually work.

**Folders 10 and 11 are the AI layer** (Week 4 retrieval, Week 5 assistant). They need a chat provider on the AI service (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or `LLM_PROVIDER=ollama`), and the assertions are written to hold on any of them. Stream requests have a Visualize tab. See postman/README.md, section 'Testing the AI assistant with Postman'.
